rate limits). Like ACMEEmail it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

tools.name: put_v1_integrations_github_repos_repo_pages
tools.description:
Sets or clears the custom domain (cname) and updates HTTPS
enforcement, build type, or source. ONLY the provided fields are sent to GitHub,
so an update never resets a setting the caller did not mention.

branch.description: Branch switches the legacy source branch. Empty leaves the source alone.

buildType.description: BuildType switches the builder: "legacy" or "workflow". Empty leaves it.

cname.description:
CNAME is the custom domain. Omit to leave it alone, "" to clear it, or a
valid FQDN to set it.

httpsEnforced.description: HTTPSEnforced toggles GitHub's enforce-HTTPS bit. Omit to leave it alone.

path.description:
Path is the source directory to pair with Branch: "/" (the default) or
"/docs". Read only when Branch is given.

repo.description: Repo is the repository, from the :repo path segment.

tools.name: put_v1_legal_templates_id
tools.description:
SaveLegalTemplateOverride saves the org's own version of a template — a custom
NDA, a house MSA — and returns it with its new version number. It takes effect
for that org only; other orgs keep the built-in.

Two boundaries cannot be crossed here. Overriding a built-in INHERITS its
category and its counsel-review posture, which can be raised but never dropped;
and a formation or equity template is counsel-review whatever the caller sends,
so no org can generate a securities-class document without the notice.

The body is validated on save, not at generation: a template that references an
UNDECLARED merge field is refused with 400 rather than stored and rendered blank
into a contract months later.

body.description:
Body is the text/template source. Required. Every {{.key}} it references must
be declared in Fields, or the save is refused rather than rendering a blank
into a contract later.

category.description:
Category groups the template: formation, equity, ops or sales. Optional when
overriding a built-in, which supplies its own.

counselReview.description:
CounselReview marks a template whose documents must carry the counsel notice.
It can be raised but never lowered: a formation or equity template is always
counsel-review, and an override of a counsel-review built-in stays one.

fields.description:
Fields declares the merge fields the body consumes. Every declared field is
REQUIRED at generation — the engine fails closed on a missing one.

id.description:
ID is the template to override, from the path. Overriding a built-in id
inherits that built-in's category, title and counsel-review posture.

title.description: Title is the template's display name. Required unless a built-in supplies it.

tools.name: put_v1_marketing_calendar_id
tools.description:
Replaces a post's editable fields. It is a full write, not
a patch, and it RESETS the lifecycle from the schedule: a scheduledAt makes
the post "scheduled" again and none makes it a draft — so editing a failed
post requeues it rather than leaving it stuck.

body.description: Body is the post text. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the target network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube or threads. Required — a post must name where it goes.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

error.description:
Error is the exact reason the last publish attempt failed — the honest
record behind a "failed" status, never a faked success.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

publishedAt.description: PublishedAt is when the publish succeeded; 0 until it does.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix publish time; 0 leaves the post a draft, and any
value makes it "scheduled" for the durable sweep to pick up.

status.description: Status is draft, scheduled, published, failed or canceled. Server-owned.

title.description: Title is the post's internal label, capped at 1024 bytes.

tools.name: put_v1_marketing_campaigns_id
tools.description:
Replaces a campaign's editable fields. It is a full write, not
a patch: every field takes the value in the body, and an omitted one is
cleared. The id comes from the path — the body cannot retarget another
campaign — and createdAt is never rewritten.

budget.description: Budget and Spend are minor units (USD cents), clamped to >= 0.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the campaign's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the free-text goal ("signups"), capped at 1024 bytes.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix send time; 0 means unscheduled. Setting it on a
campaign with no explicit status makes that status "scheduled".

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, scheduled, active, paused or completed.
Empty means draft.

tools.name: put_v1_mq_streams_name
tools.description:
Reconfigures an existing stream; the path names the stream, and the
immutable fields (storage, retention) must restate what they are.

max_age.description: MaxAge caps message age, e.g. "24h" or "7d"; "0" (default) is unlimited.

max_bytes.description: MaxBytes caps the stream's total stored bytes; -1 (default) is unlimited.

max_msg_size.description: MaxMsgSize caps one message's size in bytes; -1 (default) is the broker's limit.

max_msgs.description: MaxMsgs caps the number of stored messages; -1 (default) is unlimited.

name.description: Name is the stream name, unique within the org (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores).

num_replicas.description: Replicas is the number of stream replicas (1–5); this plane runs 1.

retention.description: Retention is the retention policy: limits (default), interest, or workqueue.

storage.description: Storage is the storage backend: file (default) or memory.

subjects.description: Subjects are the org-relative subjects bound to this stream (wildcards supported). Default: the stream name.

tools.name: put_v1_pubsub_jetstream_streams_stream
tools.description:
UpdateStream rewrites a stream's configuration — subjects, limits, discard —
and returns the updated stream. It is a PUT: the spec sent replaces the spec
held, with one reading for the enums a caller omits — an empty storage,
retention or discard keeps the stream's current one, because JetStream holds
storage and retention immutable and refuses a change with a 400 rather than
this door pretending it took.

stream.description: Stream is the stream to update, from the path.

tools.name: put_v1_pubsub_kv_bucket_key
tools.description:
Put sets one key to one value and returns the revision the write created.
Writes are versioned: each put is a new revision and the bucket retains up to
its History of them per key.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

value.description: Value is the value, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).

tools.name: put_v1_settings_product
tools.description:
PutSettings writes the caller org's configuration for one product and answers the
stored result, secrets masked. Secret VALUES are sealed into KMS under
orgs/{org}/settings/{product}/{key} and never touch this deployment's database;
with no KMS configured a write that carries any secret is refused whole (503)
rather than dropping it or persisting it in the clear. A secret the body omits
keeps its stored value, so a partial write never silently clears one.

config.description:
Config is the product's non-secret configuration, stored verbatim. Bounded at
64 KiB once serialized. Omit it to store an empty object.

product.description:
Product is the catalog slug, from the PATH. zip binds the path last, so the
URL names the product being written whatever a body field claims.

secrets.description:
Secrets are the secret fields, by name. Each VALUE is sealed into KMS and
never reaches this deployment's database; a value that is empty or equal to
the mask the read path returns means "unchanged" and is skipped, so a console
round-trip cannot blank a stored secret. A key must match
^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$, a value is bounded at 8 KiB, and an org may hold
at most 64 secret fields per product.

tools.name: put_v1_templates_slug
tools.description:
Overwrites the caller org's OWN starter kit at the path slug, answering
the stored kit. A slug they do not own is 404, never a create: the UPDATE binds
org, so a PUT can never reach another org's kit.

framework.description: only when it differs from the template's

id.description: selector, unique within the template ("react", "grid-3-fluid")

kind.description: the axis it varies: format | page | theme

source.description: the repository this shape is forked from; the synthesized default shape carries the template's own

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

description.description: Description is the browse-card blurb, max 4096 characters.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

framework.description: Framework is the stack the kit is built on ("Next.js 14").

preview.description: Preview is the still image the browse card renders, max 4096 characters.

slug.description: Slug is the kit to replace, from the path.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

tools.name: put_v1_tools_activation
tools.description:
PutActivation switches tools on and off for the caller's org and project, and
answers with the resulting activated set. It is the ONE write path that turns
skills, plugins and connectors into callable tools — an unactivated tool is
listed by discovery but refused 403 at dispatch. Activate is applied before
Deactivate, so a name in both lists ends up off. More than 256 toggles in one
request is refused 413.

activate.description: Activate switches these tool names on for the caller's org and project.

deactivate.description: Deactivate switches these tool names off.

tools.name: put_v1_translate_memory
tools.description:
Review records a human decision on one translation-memory entry, and returns the
entry as stored. A human write always wins over the stored value, and once it lands
at approved or published no machine write can move it again — which is what makes a
locale rebuild safe to run against reviewed work.

The org is ALWAYS the validated principal's org, never a request field, so a review
can only ever land in the caller's own memory.

glossary.description:
Glossary is the terminology the entry was translated under. Its VERSION — the
digest of the sorted terms — is part of the entry's identity, so editing a term
yields a new entry rather than overwriting the old rendering.

source.description:
Source is the ORIGINAL string this entry translates. Required; part of the
entry's identity, so a different source is a different entry.

state.description:
State is the entry's new position on the review ladder: suggested, approved or
published. `machine` is engine-only and is refused here — a human may not demote
a string back into the churn.

target.description:
Target is the target language tag (BCP-47, e.g. "es" or "pt-BR"). Required;
part of the entry's identity.

text.description:
Text is the reviewed translation to store. A human write always wins over the
stored value.

tier.description:
Tier is the engine tier the entry belongs to, quality (the default) or bulk.
Part of the entry's identity: the two tiers keep separate renderings.

tools.name: put_v1_usage_leaderboard_optin
tools.description:
PutUserOptin sets the CALLER's own public-listing preference on the leaderboard.
Self only: the row written is keyed by the caller's validated ledger identity, so
this can never edit another member's visibility whatever the request says. A
caller opting in with no handle is given their username, so a listed row never
renders as "Anonymous" to its own owner.

handle.description:
Handle is the display name shown on a listed row: 1-40 characters of letters,
digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a listing
opt-in it defaults to the caller's username.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the caller's row to other viewers of the board when true, and
anonymizes it when false.

tools.name: put_v1_usage_leaderboard_optin_org
tools.description:
PutOrgOptin sets the ORG's listing on the cross-org global board. Only an admin of
the caller's own org — an org admin or a platform SuperAdmin — may change it, and
the org written is the caller's validated tenant, never a value from the request.
Listing consents to publishing the org's usage VOLUME; cross-org spend stays
restricted to platform admins regardless.

display.description:
Display is the name shown for the org on that board: 1-40 characters of
letters, digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a
listing opt-in it defaults to the org id.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the org on the cross-org global board when true, and withdraws
it when false.

tools.name: put_v1_webhooks_id
tools.description:
Replaces the editable fields of one of the caller org's
endpoints — url, events, status and description — and answers the stored row
with its secret redacted. It is a full replace, not a patch: an omitted field
is written as its empty value, and an omitted or empty events list resubscribes
the endpoint to EVERY event. The signing secret and the creation time are
immutable here; rotate the secret with POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret.

description.description: Description is a free-text label for the console. Optional, clipped to 1024 bytes.

events.description:
Events are NATS subject patterns to subscribe to. An empty or omitted list
means EVERY event. Max 64 patterns, each max 256 bytes.

status.description: Status is "active" or "disabled". Empty defaults to active.

url.description:
URL is the https:// address each matching event is POSTed to. Required,
max 2048 bytes; http:// and every other scheme is refused.

tools.name: put_v1_world_pipeline
tools.description:
Replaces the caller project's news pipeline and returns what was
stored. It is a WHOLE replacement, not a patch: a field the request leaves out is
stored empty, so sending only feeds clears the filters.

Every feed URL is validated HERE, at the write boundary — http(s) only, and the
host must be on the server's allowlist — so a stored pipeline can never name a
host the fetcher would later refuse, and the allowlist is one decision in one
place rather than a check at each fetch.

keywords.description:
Keywords keeps only items whose TITLE contains one of these,
case-insensitively. They are also the GDELT queries the feed fans out to,
one per keyword of three characters or more — so a keyword both widens what
is fetched and narrows what is kept.

regions.description:
Regions keeps only items whose TITLE contains one of these, matched
case-insensitively as a substring. Empty keeps every region.

sources.description:
Sources keeps only items whose outlet name contains one of these,
case-insensitively. Empty keeps every outlet.

feeds.description:
Feeds is the RSS/Atom feed URLs to read, at most 64. Each must be an
http(s) URL whose host is on the server's allowlist — the SSRF guard is
applied here, at the write, so a stored pipeline can never name a host the
fetcher would refuse. Blank entries are dropped and duplicates collapse.

filters.description:
Filters narrows the merged feed. Terms are trimmed, de-duplicated
case-insensitively, and capped at 64 per axis.

tools.name: recordFleetSample
tools.description:
Records a BYO worker's live GPU utilization into the SAME series the
fleet board overlays. The org is the validated principal and source/kind are fixed
server-side, so a worker names only its own metrics — never another tenant or
another source. Answers 202: the warehouse write is DETACHED (its own bounded
context, never in the response path), so a slow or absent warehouse cannot stall a
heartbeat.

gpuUtil.description:
GPUUtil is accelerator utilization as a fraction 0..1; the warehouse clamps
anything outside that.

gpus.description:
GPUs is how many accelerators the reading covers, GPUModel the representative
model name.

host.description: Host is the node's hostname, for display.

memUsed.description: MemUsed and MemFree are host memory in bytes.

unit.description:
Unit is the reporting node's own id — the same id it registered under, and
the key the board joins this series onto. Required.

tools.name: scaleNodePool
tools.description:
Resizes a node pool to an absolute node count and returns the pool as
Visor reports it after the change.

clusterId.description: ClusterID and PoolID address the pool, from the URL path.

count.description:
Count is the node count to scale TO — an absolute target, not a delta, and
never negative.

provider.description: Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on. Required; body or ?provider=.

tools.name: unbindMachineAgent
tools.description:
Detaches the agent runtime from one of the caller org's
machines. The machine stays — this halts the bot, it does not terminate the
compute. Answers 204.

id.description:
ID is the machine's org-scoped NAME — the stable key Visor addresses a
machine by (owner/name), not the ephemeral provider id.
